subject: English
unit: Spring 2: The Tempest (Shakespeare): transformation through forgiveness
source: Written for english/y7 lesson 26 (Register sort and editing tasks (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 26: Grammar: formal and informal language (register). Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

head: Informal
Formal
rows: full forms: it is, does not

cards: The storm is presented as violent and uncontrollable.
Shakespeare suggests that rank means nothing at sea.
The Boatswain doesn't care about the king.
The Boatswain's commands reveal his authority.
blocks.title: Sort into: Formal / Informal
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Formal, Informal.
blocks.answer: Formal: The storm is presented as violent and uncontrollable.; Shakespeare suggests that rank means nothing at sea.; The Boatswain's commands reveal his authority.. Informal: The storm is proper scary.; The Boatswain doesn't care about the king.; Basically, everyone's freaking out.

model.title: Upgrade: 'The Boatswain doesn't care about the king and it's well funny.'

parts.text: Remove contractions: does not, it is
Use the writer's name and a method: 'Shakespeare presents...'

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Shakespeare presents the Boatswain as indifferent to the King's status, which is darkly comic and reveals that rank means nothing in a storm.

keywords.def: how formal or informal language is
the accepted grammar of formal English
a shortened word such as 'don't' for 'do not'
very informal words used in casual speech

questions.q: Rewrite formally: 'Miranda's dead upset about the ship.'
questions.a: Miranda is deeply distressed by the shipwreck.

questions.q: Rewrite formally: 'The nobles are getting in the way and stuff.'
questions.a: The nobles obstruct the sailors as they fight to save the ship.

questions.q: Core: rewrite the informal paragraph on the pupil PDF in formal Standard English (portal response box). Starter: 'In the opening scene, Shakespeare presents...'
questions.a: A formal paragraph with no contractions or slang, using 'Shakespeare presents' and 'suggests'.

questions.q: Extend: write one formal sentence about Prospero using 'reveals'.
questions.a: For example: Prospero's control of the storm reveals his immense power.

questions.q: Stretch: when might informal language be the right choice in writing?
questions.a: In dialogue for a character, a text to a friend, or to create a chatty voice deliberately.

options: Prospero is presented as powerful and controlling.
questions.a: C) Prospero is presented as powerful and controlling.. C uses full forms, the writer's method and precise vocabulary; B and A use slang and contractions.

questions.q: Answer the ponder: why do we change how we speak?
questions.a: Because audience and purpose change; formal situations need respect and precision.
